newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in bullish mood. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in bullish mood. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday on expectations of lower interest rates and a tighter supply of bonds, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct to 105.99
Volume including Makams was 195 million shekels.

"The positive atmosphere continued today in all bonds," said a trader. "Demand for unlinked bonds continues and there was a positive trend in CPI-linked bonds as well. The CPI-linked long bonds had a greater rise than the short-term ones."

"What is influencing the market are expectations that real interest rates will eventually fall, that there will not be a flood of bonds in the market because of the budget (surpluses) and because privatisation is proceeding," the trader said.
Three months of budget surpluses and increased privatisation revenues have enabled the government to raise less debt, tightening the supply of bonds, traders said.
"Money is entering the market for all kinds of bonds, and it is new money, not a change in the composition of the portfolios," said Tiki Hadad (corrects name) of IBI Investment House.
She said the fact that Sunday's 150 million shekel, 15-year CPI-linked issue had been snapped up at high prices had given a push to the market.

"The central bank stopped issuing the 15-year CPI-linked bond at the height of the provident fund crisis last year," she said. "The fact that it has resumed issuing the bonds and that the issue was absorbed well means that people are not afraid anymore and are willing to take risks on long-term bonds."
Prices of dollar-linked bonds rose on expectations of a devaluation of the shekel. "People feel something is about to happen to the dollar," a trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
